title: Signed-Capture Verified UGC for DTC Ads
one_liner: A capture SDK and verification API that proves a testimonial video came from a real, purchasing customer, for brands exposed to the FTC's fake-review rules.
customer: DTC and e-commerce brands spending on paid social, UGC agencies and marketplaces, and performance-marketing agencies with legal exposure.
problem: The FTC's rule on fake reviews and testimonials (effective Oct 2024) covers AI-generated testimonials from people who do not exist, with civil penalties above $50k per violation. AI 'UGC ad' generators now produce fake customers, and creators can deliver them through marketplaces without the brand knowing. Brands want real customers for conversion and cannot tell the difference.
solution: A web and native capture flow that records a testimonial with device attestation (Apple App Attest, Play Integrity), a random liveness phrase and a signed C2PA manifest, linked to a verified purchase through a Shopify order token. It outputs a 'Verified Real Customer' badge and an evidence file per ad. A batch API scans videos delivered through other tools, attests what can be attested and flags what cannot.
why_now: The FTC rule is in force, platforms are labeling AI content, and avatar-UGC volume has exploded. Provenance signals in phones and the C2PA ecosystem make signed capture cheap.
revenue_model: $3-8 per verified video, $500-3k/month agency plans, and a Shopify app subscription.
non_obvious_insight: The authenticity premium is really a compliance premium. Liability sits with the brand rather than the avatar vendor, so a legal-risk budget pays for it, not a marketing budget.
first_30_days: Ship a web capture flow linked to Shopify order tokens before any native SDK. Recruit 10 DTC brands through Shopify communities and UGC agencies at $5 per video, and run one campaign comparing verified and unverified creatives.

title: Buy the Restaurant Alley: Used-Oil Route Roll-Up
one_liner: Consolidate small used-cooking-oil haulers into one AI-run route business, then sell every other mandated back-of-restaurant service from the same truck.
customer: Independent restaurants and small chains (who now get paid for their oil and buy add-on services), renewable diesel and SAF refiners buying traceable domestic feedstock, and retiring collector owners selling their routes.
problem: From 2026 the 45Z clean-fuel credit applies only to North American feedstock, and UCO prices have run at roughly $1,000 to $1,400 per tonne. Restaurants historically gave oil away under auto-renewing contracts with big renderers, and theft is common. Small collectors lack chain-of-custody paperwork and contamination grading, and refiners want traceable domestic supply.
solution: Acquire 8 to 15 small collectors, grease-trap pumpers and hood cleaners in one metro. AI ops: fill-level sensors or photo estimates to cut truck miles 25% to 40%, vision-based contamination grading at pickup, automatic chain-of-custody and sustainability documentation for refiners, and a contract-reading agent that finds competitors' termination windows and times win-back offers. Add hood cleaning, grease-trap pumping and fire-suppression inspection on the same route visits.
why_now: 45Z limits credits to North American feedstock from 2026, which makes domestic UCO scarce and valuable, and documentation that used to be optional is now a selling point. Owners of small routes are aging out, and route-optimization and photo-grading tools are cheap.
revenue_model: Spread on oil resale to refiners with a share paid to restaurants, plus $150 to $500 per add-on service visit, plus a traceability premium from refiners.
non_obvious_insight: The real asset isn't the trucks; it's the contract calendar. Thousands of evergreen grease agreements with 30 to 90 day cancellation windows can be read, mapped and timed. The alley visit is also the cheapest customer touchpoint for every other mandated back-of-house service.
first_30_days: Approach a retiring one-truck collector about a seller-financed purchase in the $200k to $600k range, or start as a broker with a subcontracted truck offering 20 to 30 restaurants a paid pickup. Build a photo-based intake and contract tracker. Target franchisee groups with 5 to 10 units. Pre-sell forward oil volume to a regional biodiesel or renewable diesel refiner using documented chain of custody.

title: Modern Lodges for Fraternal Insurers
one_liner: A Lodge-as-a-Service company that builds young-adult chapters for existing fraternal benefit societies, pairing initiation ritual and mutual aid with their insurance licence.
customer: Fraternal benefit societies (roughly 200 in the US, with about $328B in assets and nearly 8 million members per industry figures) that need younger members, and the millennials and Gen Z members who pay dues.
problem: State law requires fraternal benefit societies to operate through a lodge system with regular meetings and ritual, yet lodge participation and the median member's age have both drifted the wrong way. Meanwhile lonely young adults, especially men, have almost no places built on commitment, mutual aid and belonging, and few own life or disability coverage.
solution: A branded 'new lodge' layer under an existing society's licence: chapters for a specific tribe such as tradespeople, first responders or new fathers. Each has a modern initiation ritual, monthly 'work nights' of volunteer building, a small mutual-aid fund, and a term-life or disability product sold through the society. We provide recruiting, chapter software, ritual scripts and host training.
why_now: The male-loneliness conversation peaked in 2024-26, and run clubs and other third places prove appetite for group belonging. Fraternal insurers hold the capital and the licence but have lost the recruiting engine, and most have never tried a modern chapter model.
revenue_model: Per-member acquisition fee of roughly $200-500, a revenue share of first-year and renewal premium (for example 10-20%), and chapter software and licensing fees per month.
non_obvious_insight: The scarcest asset for a startup building community plus mutual aid is an insurance licence, and the scarcest asset for a fraternal insurer is young community. Fraternal law makes ritual and lodges a regulatory requirement, so what looks like cost and cringe to a founder is actually a moat. The two parties need each other and neither can buy the other's asset.
first_30_days: Email membership and innovation directors at 30 mid-sized societies. Launch one pilot lodge in a single city with 25 founding members and a paid 'charter night'. Secure a letter of intent from one society to share premium revenue.

title: Market Surveillance for Entertainment Prediction Markets
one_liner: Sportradar-style integrity monitoring for the boom in prediction-market contracts on awards, charts, box office and game releases, where insiders and bot farms can swing outcomes.
customer: CFTC-regulated prediction-market exchanges and brokers that list entertainment contracts (Kalshi-type venues and the betting and brokerage firms entering the space). Secondary buyers are rights holders and award bodies (studios, labels, game publishers, guilds) that want to know when their confidential information is being traded.
problem: Per the briefing, Kalshi went from about $11B to $22B valuation in 2026, entertainment and awards are already about 11% of its activity, and states are fighting the venues. Exchanges must list contracts that are not readily susceptible to manipulation and run surveillance, but their tooling is built for sports and finance. Entertainment outcomes can be moved by insiders (PR staff, awards accountants, streaming-platform employees, contractors who know game release dates), by bot-farmed streams and votes, by review-bombing, and by leaked builds and schedules. Resolution sources (Spotify charts, Rotten Tomatoes, Steam counts, box office) are each gameable in a different way.
solution: (1) A 'contract risk review' done before an entertainment market lists: score the resolution source for manipulability (cost to swing it, for example streams or votes needed) and the insider population (who knows the outcome and how many people), then recommend rules such as delayed settlement, position limits and source hierarchies. (2) Live surveillance that flags anomalous trading, such as fresh accounts trading ahead of announcements or positions timed with leak or stream-spike signals, cross-referenced with external manipulation indicators (streaming bot networks, vote farms). (3) Investigation and referral packages for exchanges and regulators. (4) A rights-holder subscription that alerts when a contract references their confidential events.
why_now: Kalshi's valuation doubled in five months and new entrants are listing culture contracts. Multiple states are attacking event contracts, so demonstrable surveillance is now a legal-defense asset. GTA VI launches 19 Nov 2026 and Q4 award season and Spotify Wrapped create dense culture-contract activity. AI-cheap bot streaming and vote farms lower manipulation costs, and Chainalysis notes scam tooling now sells for about $50 (per briefing).
revenue_model: Annual retainer of $60-250k per exchange for the surveillance feed. $2-10k per contract risk review. Rights-holder alert subscriptions of $2-5k/month. Hourly investigation and expert-witness work.
non_obvious_insight: Sports-integrity firms never learned how an awards accountant or a streaming intern leaks, and entertainment insiders are far more numerous and less regulated than athletes. Resolution sources are commercial dashboards, not referees. The buyer's budget is really a legal-defense budget for defending the product state by state.
first_30_days: One fraud/market-abuse analyst plus one music/film/game data specialist. Publish a 'manipulation cost' analysis of the 10 most-traded entertainment contracts (Oscar categories, Spotify top artist, Steam concurrent players, Rotten Tomatoes scores) and send it to compliance heads at 5 exchanges. Offer a 30-day paid pilot review of upcoming contracts (GTA VI launch, award season) at $10-15k.

title: Drone-Checked Eruv Boundaries
one_liner: Scheduled autonomous drone inspection of the utility-wire boundaries that define an eruv, so communities learn before Shabbat whether a line is down.
customer: Eruv committees and synagogues in the US and abroad (hundreds of communities), plus Jewish federations and city-level committees.
problem: An eruv's boundary is often miles of utility wire, checked weekly by volunteers on foot or by car. A break invalidates carrying on Shabbat, and storms and tree limbs cause breaks. Utilities do not notify committees.
solution: Weekly autonomous flights (drone-in-a-box under Part 107 first, then BVLOS), computer-vision detection of wire discontinuity and pole damage, and GPS-pinned photo alerts to the committee. The rabbinic authority stays the decision-maker, and the tool provides the time-stamped evidence.
why_now: The FAA's Part 108 BVLOS rule cleared to OIRA (final review) in July 2026 and was not yet published as of mid-September. Drone docks and vision models are cheap. A 2016 proposal in Israel showed interest but no commercial product surfaced.
revenue_model: $300-1,500/month per eruv plus a setup fee, then adjacent inspection contracts (cemetery and campus perimeters, congregation roofs and steeples).
non_obvious_insight: The religious need is verification, not construction. A weekly audit trail with time-stamped imagery is exactly what a committee needs for its Friday declaration, which converts a religious-legal requirement into a recurring inspection budget line.
first_30_days: Contact 5 eruv committees (for example Baltimore, Teaneck, Cleveland). Fly VLOS segments with a Part 107 pilot, build a wire-break detection dataset, and sign 2 paid pilots at about $250/month.

title: W-2 Employer-of-Record for AI-Training Experts
one_liner: A task-metered payroll, benefits and contract layer that lets data vendors and labs engage expert contractors as short-term employees without the misclassification and breach exposure of 1099 mass onboarding.
customer: Second-tier human-data vendors (challengers to the Mercor-scale players) and enterprise AI teams running expert-evaluation programs pay an 8-12% margin over payroll.
problem: A class action alleges Surge AI misclassified annotators, Mercor's reported breach exposed about 40k contractors' voice samples, and contractors report declining pay and stress. Enterprise buyers in banking and healthcare won't sign vendors lacking employment and security controls. Standard EOR services can't handle 2-40 hour micro-engagements.
solution: Instant W-2 onboarding across 50 states, with per-task hourly pay, automatic state paid-sick-leave accrual, workers' comp and unemployment tax handled. A data-security wrapper (SSO, ephemeral biometric handling) and portable pay stubs for the worker's income verification round it out.
why_now: Misclassification suits and breach fallout landed in 2025-26, enterprises are now buying expert data and demanding compliance, and a multi-million expert contractor pool has appeared with unprecedented scale.
revenue_model: 8-12% of payroll plus a per-worker admin fee.
non_obvious_insight: Leading marketplaces prefer contractor status because they keep 30-40%, but enterprise and regulated buyers can't absorb the liability. Being the plumbing for challengers, not another marketplace, gives them the enterprise wedge against incumbents.
first_30_days: White-label an existing PEO or EOR to avoid licensing. Sign two small vendors (legal, medical or finance data) for a pilot cohort of 50 W-2 experts. Publish a misclassification-risk checklist to generate inbound.

title: Verified Colony-Strength Ledger for Commercial Beekeepers
one_liner: Third-party hive-strength verification and escrowed pollination contracts, turning bees into a gradeable, financeable commodity after record die-offs.
customer: Migratory commercial beekeepers running 1,000+ hives who truck colonies to California almonds and other crops. Almond and fruit growers are the counterparties.
problem: Surveys found commercial operations lost an average of about 62% of colonies between June 2024 and February 2025, and estimated the lost almond pollination income at more than $400M. Pollination is sold by phone brokers on 'frames of bees' standards that are verified by spot manual inspection, so disputes and 'strength laundering' are common. Growers can't be sure what they get, beekeepers can't prove what they have, and lenders and insurers can't underwrite either.
solution: An inspector network using thermal imaging and frame-count sampling to grade colony strength before loading, with results stored in a tamper-evident ledger tied to each yard and hive. Strength-tiered pollination contracts with escrowed payments released on verified counts. Later, hive collateral reports for ag lenders, and parametric or indemnity cover for winter losses.
why_now: The 2024-25 losses were the worst on record, and 2025-26 survey and industry reports show continuing stress. Almond growers are paying about $181 per colony (2023 figure) for strong hives and demand certainty. Thermal and camera-based frame counting is now cheap. Almond bloom in February 2027 is about five months away, so a working pilot can earn first revenue this winter.
revenue_model: $4-8 per hive inspected, paid by the beekeeper and often co-paid by growers. A 2-3% fee on escrowed contract value. Later: data fees from ag lenders and insurance commissions.
non_obvious_insight: A beekeeper's scarcest asset is now the healthy colony, and the trade runs on trust and handshake grading. A neutral, standardized 'strength certificate' does three things at once: it lets strong operators charge more, it lets growers verify what they bought, and it creates the collateral data that lets banks lend against bees. The verifier becomes the exchange.
first_30_days: Contact 5-10 mid-size migratory beekeepers and 2-3 pollination brokers now (before winter loading). Hire or contract 2-3 experienced bee inspectors, and pilot thermal frame counting on 2,000 hives. Offer growers a paid 'verified load' program for the January-February 2027 loading window. Publish a strength-grade standard and get 2 growers to commit to tiered pricing.

title: Legal Hold and Discovery for Agent Traces
one_liner: Custodian mapping, hold notices and defensible export for the agent logs that are becoming the new email in litigation.
customer: Litigation-support teams at mid-size law firms and corporate legal-ops or GC teams at companies running agents, with boutique e-discovery providers as a channel.
problem: Agent traces (prompts, tool calls, retrievals, memory) sit in observability tools and vendor consoles with retention defaults of days to weeks. They are not on custodian charts, and at least one court has treated AI-generated content as discoverable, exposing parties to Rule 37(e) spoliation sanctions. EDRM and law-firm alerts in mid-2026 say agent logs become evidence when agents fail, but nobody sells the plumbing.
solution: Connectors to Langfuse, LangSmith, OpenTelemetry and S3 stores, agent platform APIs and cloud logs. They inventory where traces live, generate agent custodian maps, flag legal holds and suspend deletion where APIs allow, snapshot with hash chains, redact PII and privileged material, and export to Relativity, Everlaw or Reveal. Add hold-aware deletion to reconcile GDPR erasure requests with active holds, and a Rule 26(f) checklist.
why_now: Agents moved into production across 2026, and the discovery literature has just started addressing agent traces. Observability vendors optimized for developer debugging (short retention, cheap storage), which is the opposite of what litigation needs.
revenue_model: $2-10k per matter plus $1-3k/month per connected source, with revenue share for e-discovery channel partners.
non_obvious_insight: E-discovery vendors will need new data sources the way they needed Slack and Teams connectors. Whoever owns the connectors to agent trace stores becomes the toll gate, and forensics tools that reconstruct incidents are not litigation-grade preservation.
first_30_days: Build 3 connectors (Langfuse, LangSmith, OpenTelemetry/S3) and a one-page hold notice and agent custodian questionnaire. Recruit 3 boutique litigation-support firms as pilots and sell a $5k agent ESI readiness assessment to GCs.

title: Street-Level Gas Pipe Retirement Optimizer
one_liner: Software plus a turnkey block-by-block electrification crew that tells gas utilities which streets to retire instead of replace.
customer: Regulated gas distribution utilities in MA, NY, CO, MN, WA, CA and IL, and their regulators. Funding comes from pipe-replacement capex budgets.
problem: Electrification shrinks gas throughput, so fixed pipe costs land on fewer customers. Utilities still replace leak-prone mains at millions of dollars per mile. Regulators (for example Massachusetts DPU 20-80-B) demand non-pipeline alternatives, but nobody optimizes at street-segment level. Heat pump quotes run ~$9,000 and labor is scarce.
solution: GIS, billing and housing-stock analytics that score each pipe segment for retire-versus-replace, and find streets where electrifying 30-80 homes costs less than replacing the main. Then deliver the electrification block by block: group purchase, one crew per street per week, optionally networked geothermal. It is filed as a utility non-pipeline alternative.
why_now: State non-pipeline-alternative orders and thermal-energy-network laws are in force. With federal credits dead, utility-funded programs are the only scaled electrification channel. Ratepayer affordability pressure makes stranded pipe a live issue.
revenue_model: $250-500k a year SaaS per utility plus a per-home program fee ($5-12k) paid from avoided pipe capex.
non_obvious_insight: Gas utilities' problem is no longer selling heat pumps. It is stranded pipe. Their pipe replacement capex is the electrification budget hiding in plain sight.
first_30_days: Model one Massachusetts or New York utility territory from public leak-prone-pipe, assessor and census data. Publish a 'retire-first streets' list for one city. Pitch a city sustainability office, a regulator and two utility strategy VPs. Sell a $60-100k pilot analysis.

title: Compliance Runtime and Audit for AI Wellness Apps
one_liner: One API that applies each state's rules for companion and wellness chatbots by user location, logs the evidence, and produces the audit reports regulators and insurers ask for.
customer: Developers of AI companion, coaching, journaling and wellness apps (thousands, mostly under 50 staff), paying $1,500-6,000 a month plus $10-25k for annual audits.
problem: Illinois banned AI in therapeutic roles (Aug 2025). California SB 243 requires AI disclosure, suicide-ideation protocols, break reminders for minors and annual reporting to the Office of Suicide Prevention from July 2027. New York, Nevada and Utah each differ. China has proposed mandatory human handoff and audits. Trump's EO 14365 seeks preemption but is contested. Pennsylvania sued over bots claiming medical licenses. Small teams cannot track this.
solution: An SDK or proxy between app and model with a geo-aware rules engine (disclosures, minor protections, banned claims, crisis protocol), a quarterly red-team and sycophancy/crisis-handoff test suite reviewed by a clinician panel, immutable logs, and auto-generated regulator and insurer reports. A clinician-signed audit letter is the certification.
why_now: SB 243 took effect in Jan 2026, first enforcement landed in May 2026, and preemption fights make the future patchwork unpredictable. Raine and similar suits make insurers and enterprise buyers ask for evidence of safeguards.
revenue_model: SaaS priced by monthly active users, annual audit fee, and per-report fees. Enterprise tier for platforms that host third-party wellness bots.
non_obvious_insight: Preemption uncertainty is a feature. Nobody will hard-code a compliance posture that may flip in 12 months, so a rules-as-configuration layer with evidentiary logs is the durable asset, not any single law.
first_30_days: Build a counsel-reviewed rulebook for CA, NY, IL, NV, UT, PA and the China draft. Scan 100 app-store companion and wellness apps for gaps and email personalized gap reports. Sell five audits at about $5k each.

title: Agent-Buyable Assay Storefronts With QC-Gated Escrow
one_liner: Turn idle university cores and orphaned biotech labs into machine-buyable assay shops where payment releases automatically only if the raw instrument data passes pre-agreed control checks.
customer: Sellers are university core facilities, small CROs and shuttered-biotech labs with idle instruments. Buyers are protein-design, synbio and 'AI scientist' teams whose agents generate thousands of candidates. Revenue comes from a take rate on transactions.
problem: Design-build-test is now bounded by assays, not DNA (the Weizmann 2.5 billion antibody fragments cost only EUR 38,000 in DNA synthesis). Yet bench services are sold by 'request a quote' forms and PDF emails that agents cannot use, and buyers cannot judge whether a result is real. NIH turbulence (grant caps, K99 restrictions, staff protections stripped) and biotech layoffs (15,000+ cuts) leave cores and dead-company labs with idle capacity and no sales function. Agent commerce already shows the pattern: RentAHuman had about 590,000 sign-ups against about 11,300 bounties, so supply is abundant and trusted demand is scarce.
solution: Each standardized assay (BLI/SPR binding, thermal shift, expression titer, mycoplasma test, mass-spec ID, sequencing verification) becomes an MCP or ACP offer with price, turnaround, sample requirements, shipping label and acceptance criteria. Money sits in escrow and releases when deterministic rules on the raw output pass (positive/negative control window, Z' above a threshold, expected ladder). A failure triggers an automatic rerun or refund, so no one argues about disputes.
why_now: Machine-payment rails shipped in 2026 (Stripe/Tempo MPP on March 18, x402 to the Linux Foundation in April, ACP/AP2). Frontier labs are running hundreds of parallel bio-agents. NIH funding instability is pushing cores to seek outside revenue, and biotech distress in 2026 is creating idle labs.
revenue_model: 5-10% take rate on assay orders, float and expedite fees on escrow, listing setup fees for sellers ($500-2,000), and a managed-account tier for large protein-design teams.
non_obvious_insight: The unsolved dispute problem in agentic commerce becomes tractable for physical science because instruments emit machine-checkable controls. Acceptance tests on raw files stand in for human judgment, and academic core capacity is the cheapest, most trustworthy supply pool exactly when NIH money is shaky.
first_30_days: Sign 5 cores (mass spec, BLI, sequencing, flow) and list 10 SKUs with fixed prices. Run everything semi-manually behind a simple API and Stripe. Offer $2K free-assay bounties to 10 protein-design groups (BindCraft/RFdiffusion users) and have their scripts place orders. Publish pass rates and turnaround. Charge 8% from day one.

title: Thermosphere Density Nowcasts From Mega-Constellation Orbits
one_liner: A live atmospheric-drag API that uses the drag on thousands of satellites as a planetary sensor grid.
customer: Mid-size LEO operators, space situational awareness vendors (as an OEM component), launch providers, insurers, and reentry-risk teams.
problem: Drag uncertainty is the dominant error in LEO conjunction assessment and reentry prediction. With over 10,000 Starlinks in orbit and Solar Cycle 25 storms hitting low shells, operators face false-alarm maneuvers, wasted propellant and surprise reentries. Existing density models are coarse.
solution: Assimilate public element sets and published satellite ephemerides to infer density by altitude, latitude and time. Deliver a nowcast plus a 72-hour forecast as an API and as a plug-in for flight-dynamics tools. Sell reduced false-alarm rates and better reentry windows, with validation reports.
why_now: The mega-constellation means the sensors are already in orbit and free. The briefing reports about 10,413 Starlinks. Storm risk persists near the solar maximum. New operators are moving to lower shells and need better drag forecasts.
revenue_model: $50-250k per year per operator. OEM licensing to SSA vendors. Event-based storm reports for insurers and launch providers.
non_obvious_insight: For space traffic, the sensor is not scarce, the model is. The largest calibration dataset ever assembled is flying overhead for free.
first_30_days: Build a backtest against public geomagnetic-storm episodes using open element sets, and publish accuracy versus a standard model. Offer free access to three mid-size operators and one SSA vendor in exchange for feedback and a paid pilot.

title: TAKE IT DOWN Desk for Small Platforms
one_liner: Outsourced 48-hour notice-and-removal operations (intake, requester verification, adjudication, audit logs) for forums, hosts and indie social apps.
customer: Small and mid-size platforms with user-generated content (forums, image hosts, creator platforms, community apps, dating apps) that have no trust-and-safety staff, plus web hosts and their counsel.
problem: The FTC began enforcing the TAKE IT DOWN Act on 19 May 2026, wrote to 15 large platforms including Discord, Reddit and Automattic, and lists civil penalties of $53,088 per violation. Coverage reaches forums with user content. The 48-hour clock is real, but the request process is abusable, since false takedown notices can be weaponised, and platforms must verify that the requester is the depicted person without collecting more sensitive imagery.
solution: A hosted intake endpoint and a staffed desk. It offers identity-light requester verification (hash matching in the style of StopNCII), adjudication by trained reviewers with escalation, removal of known identical copies across the customer's site, an appeal and counter-notice path, and FTC-ready audit logs. Follow-the-sun contractors with wellness support provide coverage. Requires legal review per jurisdiction.
why_now: Enforcement started in May 2026, the FTC opened a complaint portal (TakeItDown.ftc.gov), and nonconsensual deepfake volume is rising. Small platforms cannot afford in-house teams, and the statute imposes a duty to act with no penalty for false requests.
revenue_model: $500-5k per month base plus $15-40 per resolved case, with enterprise SLAs.
non_obvious_insight: The statute mandates speed but not accuracy, so the operational risk is over-removal and abuse. The product is adjudication with a paper trail, not filtering, and the buyer's fear is an FTC letter, not a bad user.
first_30_days: Sell through forum-software hosting partners, web-hosting providers and indie creator platforms. Train a contractor pool in handling sensitive imagery and stand up intake for 10 pilot communities.

title: Beaver Warranty for County Culverts and Roads
one_liner: A 5-year no-clog guarantee that keeps beavers out of culverts using flow devices and sensors, and later sells the wetlands they build to water and wildfire agencies.
customer: County and municipal public works departments, state DOTs and railroads, and later water utilities and wildfire agencies.
problem: Beavers plug culverts, flooding roads and forcing repeated trapping, dam breaching and clearing, which costs taxpayers every year and never ends because new beavers arrive. Managers have no reliable, maintenance-free alternative and little data on true costs.
solution: A fixed-price warranty that installs proven flow devices (culvert fences and pond levelers), adds low-cost water-level sensors and cameras, and covers every follow-up visit. Evidence in hand: Virginia's DOT spent more than $300,000 a year on prevention, repairs and removal before devices, versus under $45,000 for installation and $277 a year to maintain; and Billerica, MA found trapping and breaching cost $409 per site per year versus $229 for devices. Well-designed culvert fences reportedly succeed 95% of the time. Once the culvert is solved, we offer beaver dam analogs and habitat as water storage and fire refuge.
why_now: California's Beaver Restoration Program (2023) had received 26 proposals by April 2026, and CDFW grants have funded over 100 beaver dam analogs. Wildfire and drought budgets are looking for nature-based solutions. Cheap IoT level sensors make a guarantee affordable to price and monitor.
revenue_model: Installs of roughly $8-45k per site or bundle, an annual monitoring and warranty fee of $300-1,000, and later performance contracts with water and fire agencies for stored water or refuge acres.
non_obvious_insight: The county does not pay to deal with beavers, it pays for recurring emergency labor, so sell an insurance-style warranty backed by data, not a wildlife product. After the culvert is fixed, the beaver becomes a free crew building water storage that a different agency will pay for, so the same animal is a liability line item for one customer and an asset for another.
first_30_days: File public-records requests in five counties for trapping and culvert-clearing spend. Offer to fix the three worst culverts at cost in exchange for cost data and a case study, then sell sub-$50k warranties that fit under small-purchase thresholds.

title: Contingency Recovery of Unpaid Implant Carve-Outs
one_liner: Find and collect the implant and device carve-out payments that hospitals and surgery centers are owed but never bill, because the invoice lives in accounts payable and not in the billing office.
customer: Physician-owned spine and orthopedic ASCs, plus small and mid-size hospital ortho/spine/cardiac service lines, with commercial payer contracts that carve out implants. Paid 20-30% of recovered dollars.
problem: Many commercial contracts pay implants and high-cost devices separately, at invoice cost plus a markup, but only if the vendor invoice is submitted with the claim. The implant log is in the OR record, the invoice is in supply chain or AP, and the claim is built by billing. Nobody connects them. The claim goes out with L8699 or revenue code 027x lines at billed charges, and the payer pays $0 for the device or folds it into the case rate. The payment posts as 'paid', so nobody notices the loss. This is $5k-$50k per case for spine and joint work.
solution: Ingest the implant log (manufacturer, catalog and lot numbers), AP invoice PDFs (parsed with an LLM), contract carve-out terms extracted from the PDFs, and the 837/835 files. Compute expected carve-out payment versus actual, auto-assemble invoice attachments per payer rules, and file corrected claims and appeals inside timely-filing windows. Run it as a service for the first clients (manual, coder-led), then automate the matching.
why_now: CMS's CY2026 outpatient rule began phasing out the inpatient-only list and added many procedures, mostly musculoskeletal, to the ASC-covered list. More device-heavy spine and ortho cases are moving to ASCs whose small billing staffs have never dealt with carve-outs. Payers are also using AI-driven payment integrity that makes missing attachments an automatic zero.
revenue_model: 20-30% contingency on recovered carve-out payments. After the first recovery, convert to $1.5-4k/month prospective monitoring per facility.
non_obvious_insight: The loss is invisible in every standard revenue-cycle KPI. Denial rate looks fine and AR looks fine because the line paid 'as billed under the case rate'. The only way to see it is to lay the supply chain invoice next to the contract term next to the 835. Billers know it happens. Supply chain does not know payers pay for it. Finance never audits it. That gap between three departments is the earned secret.
first_30_days: Pick 10 physician-owned spine and ortho ASCs through ASCA chapters and surgeon-owner LinkedIn outreach. Offer a free 90-day lookback audit, since contingency means zero risk to them. Each needs to share 835s, implant logs, invoices and the top three commercial contracts. Do the first three audits by hand with a coder and a spreadsheet, and use the dollars found as the sales collateral. Then automate the invoice parsing.

title: Right-Size Rx: Deprescribing After GLP-1 Starts
one_liner: Pharmacist outreach that adjusts insulin, sulfonylureas and BP meds in the weeks after a GLP-1 start, sold to payers on avoided harm and drug spend.
customer: Medicare Advantage plans, Medicaid MCOs, ACOs and self-funded employers with large diabetic and hypertensive populations.
problem: Tirzepatide trial protocols recommend cutting sulfonylureas by at least 50% and basal insulin by at least 20% at start, because GLP-1 weight loss lowers glucose and blood pressure. In real practice nobody is triggered or paid to do this, so patients face hypoglycemia, hypotension and falls, while brand diabetes drugs (SGLT2s, DPP-4s) keep getting refilled.
solution: Claims-triggered (and pharmacy-partner-triggered for cash-pay fills) pharmacist outreach at days 7-28 after first fill among patients on insulin, SU or antihypertensives. Collaborative-practice protocols to adjust or recommend changes, home BP and CGM review, and a savings and safety ledger for the payer.
why_now: The Medicare GLP-1 Bridge started Jul 1, 2026 and cash pills at $149-$299 are pushing GLP-1s into older, more medicated patients. Payers are fixated on the GLP-1 price line and are missing the neighboring drug lines.
revenue_model: $2-4 per targeted member per month, or $250 per completed episode, plus a share of measurable avoided ED visits and drug savings.
non_obvious_insight: The near-term safety and cost of GLP-1s sits in the other drugs on the patient's list. Payers can offset part of the GLP-1 cost by trimming those, so it belongs on a CFO's line item, not just a quality dashboard.
first_30_days: Approach one regional MA plan or IPA and one pharmacist group. Run a 90-day pilot on 300 patients identified from Rx claims. Measure interventions made, hypoglycemia events and avoided fills, and hand back a savings ledger.

title: Notice Desk with Contingency Penalty Abatement
one_liner: Snap a photo of any IRS or state notice, get triage and a response, and pay only if the penalty is abated.
customer: 1-25 employee firms, S-corps and small partnerships that received late-filing, payroll-deposit, information-return mismatch or state tax notices.
problem: Notices sit in a drawer or a registered-agent inbox while penalties compound. Abatement routes (first-time abatement, reasonable cause, small-partnership relief) are well established but owners don't know them, and CPAs bill hourly. Filing rules are shifting: the 1099-NEC floor rose to $2,000, 1099-K thresholds reverted, and new tips and overtime reporting will create mismatches. IRS capacity appears strained (prior knowledge).
solution: Forward or photograph the notice. The system classifies it, extracts the deadline and amount, explains the options and drafts the response. An enrolled agent or CPA partner signs, files the abatement request and tracks it. State-notice variants are added by jurisdiction. A $19/month mail-monitoring plan for registered-agent customers catches new notices.
why_now: BOI filing services just lost their main product and need a new recurring hook, and compliance work is moving from filing to interpretation. LLMs can read notices at scale.
revenue_model: 20% of penalties abated, $49 flat for triage on notices with no abatement path, and $19/month monitoring.
non_obvious_insight: A penalty notice is a lead with a known dollar value. Many abatements are near-automatic, so outcome pricing beats hourly billing, and Intuit, Xero and H&R Block cannot easily price on outcomes.
first_30_days: Get 100 anonymized notices from CPA partners and registered-agent companies to train the classifier. Sign an enrolled agent, run 30 abatements sourced from small-business forums, and record the abatement rate.

title: Second-Life Desal Membranes for Farms and Towns
one_liner: Buy retired reverse-osmosis elements from big desal plants, test and recondition them, and sell them with a performance guarantee to farms, greenhouses and small systems.
customer: Brackish-water growers and greenhouse operators (Arizona, Texas, Imperial and Yuma areas), oilfield produced-water treaters, and small utilities, starting non-potable. Sellers of used elements are large plants. Buyers pay per element.
problem: Large plants replace a slice of their elements every year, and a commonly cited literature figure puts discarded RO membranes at over ten thousand tonnes annually. Small brackish and farm users pay $600-1,200 per new element and face lead times. Desal is spreading as costs fall (about $0.50/m3 typical, with a reported $0.28/m3 waste-heat plant in China that is not fully verified), and Cyprus approved an 85M euro mobile unit in April 2026.
solution: Acquire retired elements, then test flux, rejection and pressure drop. Clean and sort by remaining performance. Sell 'certified reconditioned' elements with a guarantee to non-potable users. Offer plants a take-back service (they avoid disposal cost and gain a circularity claim). Add a membrane-health monitoring subscription and, later, downcycle to nanofiltration and ultrafiltration. Potable use needs NSF certification, so leave it for later.
why_now: The desal fleet is growing worldwide, farms need cheap brackish-water treatment as river cuts arrive, and the aftermarket is untouched because of warranty fear.
revenue_model: $150-450 per reconditioned element, take-back fees from plants, and monitoring subscriptions.
non_obvious_insight: Membranes are a consumable like tires, in a growing market where everyone innovates on new chemistry and nobody tests the aftermarket. An independent test standard plus a performance guarantee turns a landfill cost into low-cost supply.
first_30_days: Contact five brackish and seawater plant operators and used-element brokers. Buy 200 used elements. Rent test-rig time from a university lab or build a $30-60k rig. Sell five trial sets to greenhouse or ag operators in Arizona or Texas.

title: Corner-Shop Human Fallback for Age Assurance
one_liner: A network of licensed retailers that check ID in person and mint reusable, privacy-preserving age credentials, sold to age-assurance vendors and platforms as the human appeal layer.
customer: Age-assurance vendors and platforms (social, gaming, adult, gambling, app stores) that face false rejections. Retailers such as independent pharmacies, post offices, newsagents, liquor stores and credit unions earn per credential.
problem: Facial age estimation has error bands near the threshold, so borderline users (16-18, and adults who look young) are blocked. Adults with expired or mismatched ID are locked out. The appeals queue is expensive support, and the legal exposure is real: Australia's under-16 social media law, in force since December 2025, carries fines up to A$49.5 million, and the UK's Online Safety Act requires highly effective age assurance.
solution: Partnered counters run a clerk app. The customer shows government ID, the app reads the chip by NFC without retaining an image, and it issues a reusable over-13, 16, 18 or 21 credential to the person's phone wallet, or a code for those without a smartphone. Platforms and vendors route estimation failures and borderline users to the nearest counter or a video-call agent through one API. Audit logs, retailer training and mystery-shop QA back the process.
why_now: Australia's guidance treats reusable age credentials, vouching and trusted third-party attestation as acceptable methods. California's app-store age assurance law takes effect on January 1, 2027, and UK enforcement has expanded through 2026. Every platform is discovering that automated estimation needs a human fallback.
revenue_model: The vendor or platform pays $0.75-2.50 per rescued user, and the retailer keeps about 40%. Add cents per reuse verification, and enterprise contracts for fallback capacity.
non_obvious_insight: Regulators demand highly effective age assurance, but nobody has built the cheap human appeal layer. Licensed retailers are already trusted age checkers for alcohol, tobacco and medicines. The network of humans is the moat, not the cryptography, and it earns as long as automated estimation is imperfect.
first_30_days: In one Australian metro, sign 40 independent pharmacies and newsagents. Build the clerk app on an open-source NFC reader for passports and licenses. Pitch two age-assurance vendors on a white-label fallback and charge per rescued user for a 60-day pilot. Track false-reject recovery rate as the headline metric.

title: Fitness-Adjusted Longevity Reports for Retirement Advisors
one_liner: A report that turns a client's own wearable and clinic metrics (VO2max, resting heart rate, grip strength, gait speed, sleep) into a life-expectancy range for Social Security claiming, annuity timing and withdrawal-rate decisions, sold to fee-only advisors.
customer: Fee-only RIAs and retirement planners serving affluent pre-retirees aged 58-70, at $75-150 per client report or $300-600 a month per advisor. Later customers are planning-software vendors and annuity carriers.
problem: Social Security is the largest lifetime asset most households own. Claiming at 70 instead of 62 raises the monthly benefit by roughly three-quarters, and the break-even sits around 80-83. That decision hinges on life expectancy, but planners use population tables. Clients in the top fitness quintile can plausibly outlive the average by several years, and the sedentary can be the opposite. Early claiming reportedly jumped in 2025 amid trust-fund and SSA-staffing fears, so many people are choosing blind.
solution: Adjust standard actuarial tables using published hazard ratios for cardiorespiratory fitness, gait speed, grip strength and resting-heart-rate trends. Output a range, not a point estimate, showing break-even age versus the chance of reaching it. Data comes in by consented export from Apple Health, Garmin or Oura and is processed locally. The PDF carries methodology and disclaimers written for advisor compliance, and it is explicitly not medical advice or insurance underwriting.
why_now: Consumer wearables now deliver near-clinical metrics, including FDA-cleared hypertension notifications on Apple Watch in 2025 and VO2max estimates on most premium devices. Basic planning software is being commoditized by AI, so advisors need differentiated inputs. A wave of early Social Security claiming in 2025 shows clients are making irreversible choices under fear. Advisors have avoided health data because of privacy concerns, but client-owned wearable data solves the consent problem.
revenue_model: Per-report pricing of $75-150, advisor subscriptions of $300-600 a month, and later white-label integrations with planning tools. Annuity carriers may pay for qualified leads.
non_obvious_insight: Planners have been told for decades to plan for longevity risk while seeing only age and sex, and wearables have quietly built the best individual mortality signal outside a hospital. A plus or minus 4-year shift is enough to move the claiming break-even, so precision is not needed. The buyer is the advisor, who needs a fiduciary-safe way to bring health into the conversation.
first_30_days: Build the calculator from published cohort studies on fitness and gait speed and a standard actuarial table, and have a consulting actuary review it for $3-5k. Run 30 free reports for eight advisors in fitness-forward niches such as physician-focused planners and FIRE planners. Collect feedback and objections. Then charge $99 a report, with no health data stored on your servers.

title: Grandschools: Microschools Inside Senior Communities
one_liner: Turnkey K-8 microschools hosted in senior-living and 55+ communities, with residents as mentors and tuition funded by ESAs and scholarship credits.
customer: Senior-living operators and 55+ communities (pay a program fee for engagement and occupancy marketing); families paying tuition, ESA or scholarship dollars; retired professionals as mentors.
problem: More than 1,000 public schools closed in 2025-26, families are being displaced, and microschools struggle to find trusted adults (at Alpha School two-thirds of guides lack teaching credentials). Senior communities struggle with purpose-driven programming and occupancy. Each side has the resource the other lacks.
solution: A franchise-lite pilot model of 12-24 kids, 1 lead guide and 6-10 resident 'grand-mentors' (retired engineers, teachers, nurses) running project blocks, sharing dining, garden and library space. A standard playbook covers background checks, safeguarding, insurance, private-school registration and a mentor-hour ledger. Enrollment through ESA and SGO scholarships.
why_now: The demographic cliff in kids meets the aging peak. Scholarship credits and ESAs from 2027 make tuition viable for middle-income families, and the microschool guide shortage is acute.
revenue_model: $6-9k per child in tuition or ESA funds; operator program fee of $1-2k a month (or free space); licensing and playbook fees when replicating.
non_obvious_insight: The two halves of the demographic shift are each other's missing input: shrinking youth cohorts leave surplus buildings, growing elderly cohorts hold surplus expertise, and aging-services operators have engagement budgets that schools have never tapped.
first_30_days: Approach 10 independent-living communities in one metro that have on-site classrooms and sign one. Recruit 10 families from closed-school parent groups and a certified guide. Launch a 'Fridays' pilot before a full schedule. Confirm state private-school registration and insurance first.

title: NOI Haircut Reports for Multifamily Underwriting
one_liner: A 24-hour diligence report that restates a multifamily property's NOI for real concessions, renewal cliffs and banned fee income, sold to the lenders and buyers who will feel it first.
customer: Debt funds, CRE CLO managers, agency-lender underwriting teams and mid-market syndicators buying 100-1,000 unit properties in concession-heavy or fee-regulated markets.
problem: Headline NOI rests on face rents and other income. Concessions run 15.8% of stabilized units and 1.2M units are still in lease-up, and leases signed with free months renew at face rent a year later, inviting churn. Fee income (admin, pet, package, parking) is being banned: Seattle from July 2027 with treble damages, and the NAA tracked 140 fee bills in 2025. Sellers' T-12s show neither risk.
solution: Upload rent roll, T-12 and fee schedule and receive net-effective rent by lease cohort, concession burn-off and renewal-cliff dates, fee income at risk by jurisdiction and effective date, and a stressed NOI and DSCR. A monitoring API flags changes across a loan book as laws pass.
why_now: Concessions are now the pricing lever because rent cuts hurt valuations and algorithmic pricing is legally constrained. Dated fee bans give lenders a hard clock, and the rental supply wave has crested, so underwriting errors will show up in 2027 renewals.
revenue_model: $750-2,500 per report; $2-5K per monitored loan per year; enterprise API licenses to lenders.
non_obvious_insight: NOI has become a policy variable, but underwriting models still treat it as a market variable. The party whose model breaks first is the lender, not the operator, and lenders have diligence budgets.
first_30_days: Build a law and effective-date database for the 10 states and cities with fee rules. Publish three public teardown case studies on listed properties. Sell $500 pilot reports to 10 syndicators via LinkedIn and BiggerPockets, then pitch two debt funds on a diligence add-on.

title: GST Credit Recovery on UPI Fees
one_liner: Recover the 18% GST on new UPI MDR fees as input credit for retailers and distributors that will otherwise never claim it.
customer: GST-registered mobile, FMCG and pharma retailers and distributors in India, and their chartered accountants.
problem: From Oct 15 the 0.4% MDR carries 18% GST, and AICPDF estimates a Rs 7,000-9,000 Cr burden on distributors. Small businesses will not reconcile bulk PSP fee invoices to GSTR-2B, so credit is left unclaimed.
solution: Ingest PSP settlement reports, match fee invoices to GSTR-2B, flag missing credits and produce claim workpapers for CAs. Composition-scheme dealers are ineligible and must be screened out. The wedge is retailer associations already mobilising over the fee.
why_now: MDR starts Oct 15 and retailer bodies are organised around a 'No UPI Day' on Oct 2.
revenue_model: 10-15% of recovered credit, or Rs 499-1,999 per month per business.
non_obvious_insight: The protest is about the 0.4%. The GST layer is partly recoverable money nobody is discussing, and associations will trade it for a visible win for members.
first_30_days: Build reconciliation for PhonePe and Paytm settlement file formats and sign two retailer associations.

title: After-School Shop Clubs Run by Retired Tradespeople
one_liner: Screen-free after-school care for ages 10-15 inside idle trade-school and union shops, staffed by retired journeymen who teach kids to build real things.
customer: Parents of 10-15-year-olds paying about $180-260 a month, plus sponsors (contractor associations, distributors, JATCs and local subs) paying $150-300 per enrolled kid as a recruiting pipeline. State child-care subsidy vouchers where the program is licensed.
problem: School-age care from 3 to 6pm is scarce, and Gen Alpha teens fill it with phones and AI companions (72% of US teens have used them) while under-16 social bans leak. Most of the trades labor gap is retirements, and the pipeline is thinner than headlines suggest (the enrollment surge is called a demographic mirage). Community-college and JATC shops sit empty after 3pm. Retired tradespeople lose purpose and have no channel to pass on skills.
solution: Run a licensed or license-exempt (per state rule) after-school program in partner shops. One certified childcare lead plus paid retired journeyman mentors ($25-30/hr from sponsor funds) run projects such as tiny houses, cabinetry, wiring boards and plumbing trees. Phones stay in lockers. Older kids earn micro-credentials (OSHA-10 at 16, NCCER Core) and sponsors get first look. A small local team can run in three shops in year one.
why_now: Australia, Brazil, Indonesia and Malaysia have under-16 bans, US school phone bans cover 12 states, and parents want credible offline options. ROAD to Housing Act standard plans and manufactured-home reforms are creating build content and demand for skilled set crews. The retirement wave is driving most of the ABC 349K and 456K worker gap.
revenue_model: Tuition $180-260 per child per month, sponsor fees $150-300 per child per month (or lump-sum program sponsorship), subsidy vouchers where eligible, and mentor stipends funded through sponsorship.
non_obvious_insight: The apprenticeship pipeline's real bottleneck is exposure and mentors before age 16, not training seats. Idle shops, retired mentors and parents desperate for screen-free care are three underused assets that pay for each other. A contractor who pays $3K to keep a local kid in the trades over two years is spending less than the cost of one bad hire.
first_30_days: Partner with one community college, ABC or IEC chapter training center. Recruit three retired journeymen and confirm the state licensing exemption (or license a school-age program). Run an 8-week pilot three afternoons a week for 12 kids at $180 a month, with $500 sponsorships from five local subs, and fill the waitlist through local parent Facebook groups.
